descripcion: Tendo brewery whose Oka Ginjo of 1980 opened the ginjo market in Japan. Works Yamagata's own rice varieties and has its own online shop.
Brewery founded in 1832 at the foot of Mount Chokai, the first in Yamagata to brew junmai daiginjo only. Its Komyo polishes the rice down to one percent.
Founded in 1597 as supplier to the Yonezawa domain and now in its twenty-fourth generation. Brews the Toko label and has its own sake museum.
Brewery of more than three hundred years in Takahata, growing part of its rice with farmers in the village. Own online shop.
Sagae brewery brewing with meltwater from Mount Gassan. Sells from its own online shop.
Brewery founded in 1898 in Tendo, now in its fifth generation. Grows its own rice and sells the Yamagata Masamune label from its own shop.
Brewery in the port of Sakata, in the Shonai district, known for the Jokigen label. Does not sell direct from its site.
Murayama brewery and home of the Juyondai label, among the most sought-after in Japan. It has no own site and sells only through appointed distributors.
Brewery in the Haguro district of Tsuruoka, known for the Kudoki Jozu label. The guild lists it with neither site nor email.
Brewery in the Higashine spa town, making sake and fruit liqueurs from the district. Own online shop.
Brewery in central Yonezawa, in the Okitama district. Sells its Kobai label from its own online shop.
Sagae brewery, a different company from Kotobuki Toraya Shuzo despite the shared Toraya. Own online shop.
Brewery in the Oyama district of Tsuruoka, with its own sake museum. Sells the Dewa no Yuki label from its online shop.
Yonezawa brewery known for the Kurozaemon and Gazanryu labels. Its site offers no direct sales.
Small brewery in the city of Yamagata, focused on aged junmai daiginjo.
Brewery in central Yamagata city. Not to be confused with the Otokoyama of Asahikawa, in Hokkaido, which is a different company.
Brewery at the foot of Mount Haguro, in Tsuruoka, brewing the Hakuro Suishu label with water from the Dewa range.
Sagae brewery with a historic building on the cultural property register. Brews the Sawa Masamune label.
Brewery at the foot of Mount Chokai, in Sakata, specializing in the traditional kimoto fermentation method.
Brewery in the city of Yamagata. Its site paints with JavaScript and could not be read as plain HTML.
Brewery in the Oyama district of Tsuruoka, label Oyama. The domain the guild publishes declares itself an old site.
